text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha promises to lower taxes for the press.

- Berisha has called on ethnic Albanians in Serbia's Kosovo region to join in student protests in Belgrade against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, but Albanians say they are better off under Milosevic than the Zajedno opposition.
- Berisha said it was legitimate for Albanian companies to offer large returns on investments but that such activities carried the risk of failure.
- Five months after the introduction of value added tax experts are saying the state budget is drawing in 2.5 times more than the previous turnover tax.

- U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation experts said no law existed in Albania to prevent money laundering. They said they suspected Albanian firms offering high returns on investments were either involved in money laundering or pyramid schemes.

- Berisha has told Pranvera Hoxha, daughter of the late communist dictator Enver Hoxha, he would not interfere with the judiciary after she asked him to guarantee the rights of her husband, who is under arrest.
- Klement Kolaneci, son-in-law of the late dictator Enver Hoxha, has staged a hunger strike from prison in protest against a ban on family members visiting him.

- Smaller opposition parties have warned they would hold a protest if demands for a new constitution, are not met by the ruling Democrats, whose parliamentary majority it claims was gained by vote rigging.

- Albanian Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu told a NATO meeting in Brussels the Dayton agreement had not managed to stabilize the Balkans and therefore Albania should become part of NATO when it expands eastwards.
- Villagers growing cannabis are regularly being caught by the police but the ringleaders organising the trafficking remain untouched.
- Hours after the signing of an agreement with Italy to stop the flow of would-be-immigrants from the Albanian coast, Albania mobilized special police and helicopters for joint patrols.
